stories.title: Senior Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
summary: The Israeli military said it had killed Abu Younis in a strike in the southern Gaza Strip overnight, adding that he had led the Rafah brigade since his predecessor, Nael Abu Obeid, was killed on September 15.
Read: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Hamas said Abu Younis joined Hamas' armed wing in 1991 and had held several senior operational roles in Rafah before becoming commander of the brigade.

Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in the military campaign that Israel launched against Gaza after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel in the October 7 attack.

stories.title: Australia retain women's Rugby League World Cup
summary: Winger Jaime Chapman collected a hat-trick as Australia crushed New Zealand 34-10 on Sunday with an emphatic first-half performance to clinch their fourth consecutive women's Rugby League World Cup.
This has definitely been a dream come true, and I knew that we could get the job done." Before Australia's global rise, New Zealand won the World Cup in 2000, 2003 and 2008.

New Zealand finally got on the board when Shannon Mato barged across, but Chapman's third, bursting two tackles to race away, put Australia back in full control before Tamika Upton added a sixth before half-time.

stories.title: Sayers says everyone knew about 'Sandpapergate'
summary: Former Australian Test bowler Chadd Sayers backed Usman Khawaja over his "Sandpapergate" claims on Sunday, contradicting Pat Cummins' denials that he knew nothing about the ball-tampering plot.
Sayers was on the tour of South Africa but did not play in the third Test at Cape Town, where sandpaper was used to help make the ball swing.
Khawaja also alleged sandpaper was used in the second Test at Port Elizabeth, with Sayers saying he was the one who took it from the field.

stories.title: Ciryl Gane downs Josh Hokit to retain UFC heavyweight title
summary: UFC heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane of France successfully defended his title for the first time, sweeping the scorecards 48-47, 48-47, 48-47 against Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in New York on Saturday night.
As Hokit's punches began to fade in Round ⁠4, Gane took control, countering the challenger's fence clinches with several body kicks, knees to the midsection and short, dirty-boxing uppercuts.

With the result still in the balance in Round 5, Gane stuffed Hokit's takedown attempts and opened a cut just above his left eye, then dominated the striking with jabs, body shots and multi-punch combinations through the end of the round.

stories.title: UPS cargo plane, Copa Airlines passenger jet collide at Miami airport in US
summary: A UPS cargo plane and a Copa Airlines passenger jet collided at Miami International Airport in the US state of Florida late on Saturday, prompting an emergency response, local media reported.

The collision occurred around 9:15pm local time (0215GMT Sunday) when an arriving aircraft and a departing plane came into contact at the intersection of two taxiways, Greg Chin, communications director at Miami International Airport, said.

The collision occurred as Miami International Airport continued to experience flight delays and cancellations following an unusual nationwide ground stop ordered on Friday by the Federal Aviation Administration.

stories.title: Officials from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Turkiye arrive in Islamabad for 30th ECO ministerial meeting
summary: Mr. Elnur Mammadov, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan and Head of Delegation, arrived in Islamabad to participate in the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting.
Mr. Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, arrived in Islamabad to participate in the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting.
He was received at Islamabad International Airport by the officers of MoFA. pic.twitter.com/dZO3XWeETf — Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) November 15, 2026 H.E.

stories.title: Mohammad Yousuf, Sana Mir inducted into PCB Hall of Fame
summary: Former Pakistan batting great Mohammad Yousuf and former women’s team captain Sana Mir have been inducted into the PCB Hall of Fame for 2025 in recognition of their outstanding performances and valuable contributions to Pakistan cricket.

Sana Mir, who became the first Pakistan woman cricketer to be inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame in 2025, has been automatically included in the PCB Hall of Fame in line with the PCB’s induction criteria.
Last year, Sana became the first Pakistan woman to be inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame, recognising her achievements and contribution to the women’s game.

stories.title: US thrash Haiti as Pochettino prepares for farewell
summary: McKennie's 68th-minute header put Pochettino's side 5-0 up and the US thought they had added a sixth soon afterwards when Balogun shrugged off Arcus to score from close range.
A VAR review, however, determined that Balogun had fouled Arcus in the build-up and the goal was chalked off.
Balogun did not have long to wait though for his 13th international goal, latching on to a Malik Tillman through ball to score in the 82nd minute.

stories.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles towards Riyadh, drones in Eastern Province
summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Sunday it had intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles launched towards the Saudi capital Riyadh and three drones in the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province.
The Houthis have stepped up strikes on ⁠Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities, while Saudi Arabia has ramped up airstrikes on Houthi targets ​in Yemen in response.
The interceptions come amid escalating hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, with repeated missile and drone attacks targeting the kingdom.

stories.title: Bahrain says its air defences intercepted several Iranian attacks
summary: Israeli military officials estimate that Iran possesses more than 1,500 ballistic missiles, although regional assessments differ, according to the report.
Iran's missile and drone attacks have continued to expose vulnerabilities in US military installations, radar systems and early-warning infrastructure across the Middle East, according to the report.

Two oil tankers hit mines, catch fire near Strait of Hormuz: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's IRGC Navy said early on Sunday.

stories.title: ATC moves to declare Afridi absconder
summary: The court ordered issuance of notices under Section 87 of the Code of Criminal Procedure after police submitted a report stating the two nominated accused could not be located.

DFC Muhammad Iqbal of East Cantonment police station informed the court that arrest warrants issued under Section 204 CrPC against Muhammad Sohail Afridi and Muhammad Aamir Khan could not be executed despite all efforts.
More than 80 accused have been nominated in the Radio Pakistan attack case, whose trial is underway in the Anti-Terrorism Court.

stories.title: CM vows no safe havens for terrorists in Balochistan
summary: Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti on Saturday declared that terrorist elements seeking to destabilise the province would not be allowed to establish safe havens, asserting that the state would employ an effective strategy to defeat terrorism and protect citizens.
Bugti was commenting on a recent security operation in the Kolpur area in which eight terrorists affiliated with the India-backed Fitna al-Hindustan were killed.

Intelligence-based operations are continuing in Kolpur, Kirdgap and Nushki, the chief minister said, while security has been further strengthened along the Quetta-Taftan National Highway to ensure the safety of citizens and uninterrupted movement of traffic.

stories.title: ANP rejects any move to divide K-P
summary: He said the ANP would not retreat even an inch from its position on protecting the province's mineral resources and ensuring their fair distribution.
He said the ANP would soon convene a meeting of its think tank to deliberate on the prevailing situation.

The ANP believes that the challenges confronting the province cannot be addressed by any single political party, he said, stressing the need for all political forces and relevant stakeholders to unite around a common minimum agenda.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks financing for household solar revolution
summary: He said Pakistan’s solar transition was increasingly being driven by households making independent investments in rooftop solar installations, often without financial assistance from the government or international institutions.
He said households had effectively created a decentralised electricity generation system, with rooftops emerging as new centres of energy production.
The emerging rooftop solar model, he added, offered an alternative in which households could generate electricity locally and store surplus power for use when sunlight was unavailable.

stories.title: Akbari Gate to reopen after two centuries
summary: The historic Akbari Gate of Lahore Fort is expected to be reopened to the public next month after remaining closed for nearly two centuries.
Located on the eastern side of the fort, the Akbari Gate had been constructed to connect the Walled City with the royal citadel.
An official, Owais Raza, said the gate would be opened to the public in December, allowing visitors to enter the fort through the historic route.

stories.title: A 37-year-old mystery, satellite image and missing aircraft
summary: Sabih Ali Rajput claims to have identified the possible remains of flight PK-404 in a remote, snow-covered mountainous region near Tajikistan, after spending two years examining satellite imagery and retracing the aircraft's final journey through Google Earth.

Rajput says his investigation involved piecing together the aircraft's route, estimated flight duration, fuel capacity and other available information before scanning satellite images of remote mountain ranges.
Rajput believes the aircraft may have attempted to turn back towards Gilgit because of bad weather.

stories.title: Unhygienic conditions at JPMC threaten safety of doctors, patients
summary: Doctors at the endoscopy ward of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) are reportedly being forced to use old and contaminated lead aprons bearing visible blood stains, raising serious concerns about the health and safety of medical staff as well as patients.
Photographs of the radiation-protection aprons being used at the hospital have emerged, showing prominent blood stains on the protective gowns and their poor hygienic condition.
According to medical sources, the same lead aprons are being used repeatedly during different medical procedures and surgeries in the endoscopy unit without regular washing and disinfection.

stories.title: Cancer meds shortage spurs speedy procurement
summary: Following special reports aired by Express News and published in Daily Express and The Express Tribune, Secretary Specialised Healthcare Punjab Azmat Mahmood convened an emergency meeting in Lahore, attended by medical superintendents of the six hospitals and relevant officials.

The health secretary issued clear instructions to complete the procurement process for the cancer medicine in the shortest possible time and restore its provision to patients through the free home delivery system so that they could receive the medicine at their doorsteps.

Upon a follow-up, the hospital spokesperson said that the RIC has performed free open-heart surgeries on 320 adult patients and cardiac procedures on 236 children under the government health programme since July 2026.

stories.title: CPO, SSP issued notices in Hina Javed case
summary: The Branch has issued notices to the City Police Officer (CPO) and the SSP Investigation, demanding an explanation and directing the immediate submission of the charge-sheet in the high-profile murder case.
The police are required to submit a charge-sheet within 14 days under the law; however, the investigative teams have failed to do so even after two months and 26 days.
According to the investigative team, the formal charge-sheet for the high-profile case is set to be submitted within the next ten days.

stories.title: Much-awaited New Blue Area parking plaza opens
summary: The parking plaza has the capacity to accommodate over 1,200 vehicles simultaneously, with services available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
According to the CDA administration, a fully digital parking system has been implemented at the parking plaza, which is also complemented by a digital monitoring system to ensure security.

Under the modern digital system, all vehicles and motorcycles entering the parking plaza will be issued receipts through a digital process and parking fees will be collected when a vehicle or motorcycle exits the facility.

stories.title: New units buzz grows after power huddle
summary: The meeting between Zardari and Sharif at the latter's Model Town residence in Lahore followed the president's earlier meeting with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in Nawabshah.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office, the two leaders discussed the country's overall political, economic and security situation.
The meetings come amid renewed debate over the creation of new provinces after Naqvi proposed that political parties seek public opinion on the issue through a referendum.

stories.title: Heavy snow cuts off key tourist route to G-B
summary: As the snowfall makes the high-altitude route inaccessible, the process of clearing snow and restoring traffic has become dependent on prevailing weather conditions.

For certain destinations, travelling via Babusar Pass takes less time than using the longer Karakoram Highway route, making it a preferred route for a large number of tourists and travellers during the summer months.
Babusar Road generally remains closed to traffic for around six months every year because of severe cold, snowfall and difficult weather conditions.

stories.title: Opp moves FCC against lawmakers' detention
summary: The opposition leaders in the National Assembly and Senate have approached the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) against the arrest and detention of PTI lawmakers in the wake of the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in K-P.
The petitioners seek the immediate release of all detained elected representatives, arguing that keeping elected representatives in custody undermines the mandate of the people.

stories.title: 'Young Stunners' bring Karachi's chaos to Coke Studio Nu.WAV
summary: Coke Studio Nu.WAV has concluded its six-song series with Diwanay Dil, bringing together Young Stunners, singer Sabaat Batin and producer Jokhay in a track that draws inspiration from Karachi's restless energy and everyday chaos.
Young Stunners, formed in 2012, have played a significant role in taking Urdu hip-hop from Pakistan's underground music scene to a wider regional audience.
Across its six releases, Nu.WAV brought together established names and emerging artists, exploring different sounds and collaborations within Pakistan's contemporary music landscape.

stories.title: World Culture Festival presents cultural melting pot
summary: From the soul-stirring strains of qawwali to the electric energy of rock music, the 17th day of the 25-day Third World Culture Festival Karachi 2026 offered audiences a vibrant celebration of musical traditions and international performing arts.
The evening's biggest draw was Bazm-e-Qawwali, where renowned Pakistani qawwals Rizwan and Muazzam held the audience spellbound at the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi's Open-Air Theatre.
With music, film and theatre sharing the stage, the festival continued to turn Karachi into a meeting point for artists and audiences from across the world.

stories.title: 'Ebenezer' leads N America weekend box office
summary: It's Depp's first major Hollywood movie since 2018's 'Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald', and Paramount spent $38 million to produce the film plus another $50 million to market it.
'Ebenezer' earned $7.1 million on Friday, including previews, and Deadline now projects a healthy $20 million-plus opening for a non-franchise Depp movie.
A domestic opening near that range would put 'Ebenezer' in line with the starts of Depp's 2015 film 'Black Mass' ($22.6 million) and 2009's 'Public Enemies' ($25.2 million).

stories.title: Govt defers ML-3 for third time
summary: The Central Development Working Party (CDWP), for the third time in the past five months, deferred approval of the Rs278 billion, or $1 billion, up-gradation of ML-3 track from Nokhandi to Rohri this month, according to the Ministry of Planning officials.

Government officials said that the project's approval had been postponed due to funding constraints and the possibility that the Reko Diq Mining Company, being run by Barrick Gold, could use Gwadar Port for the transportation of minerals.

Also, a delegation of Barrick Gold Company met with Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal this week and sought details of the road project that could be constructed, according to people privy to the discussions.

stories.title: WB okays $300m for human capital
summary: The World Bank Group's Board of Executive Directors approved $300 million in financing to expand access to safe water supply, sanitation and hygiene services for 1.5 million people in selected rural areas of Sindh.
The financing will support the Sindh Transformational Accelerated Rural Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene Services Phase 1 Project (STAR WASH-1).
STAR WASH-1 will provide 1.5 million people with access to safe water, and safely managed sanitation and hygiene services.

stories.title: Deputy collectors to lead anti-smuggling units
summary: Pakistan Customs has decided to place its anti-smuggling units under the command of assistant and deputy collectors, with a notification issued in this regard.
According to the notification, each anti-smuggling unit will be headed by an assistant or deputy collector instead of a superintendent or senior preventive officer.

Anti-smuggling squads will be led by inspectors or preventive officers, while squad in-charges will report directly to the assistant or deputy collector without going through any intermediate officer.

stories.title: China, US discuss tariffs, farm trade
summary: China and the United States discussed tariff cuts, agricultural trade and other issues at their first trade council meeting on Friday, China's Commerce Ministry said on Saturday, days ahead of an expected leaders' meeting in Shenzhen next week.

Canada, US make progress on trade deal Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Saturday he had held lengthy, substantive talks with US President Donald Trump and the two countries were making progress towards a trade deal, though they had yet to reach an agreement.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday he believed the US would secure trade deals with Mexico and Canada, a day after Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico over a migrant caravan.

stories.title: Modi's office probes website takedowns
summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office summoned the telecommunications secretary on Saturday, asking him to explain how officials ordered the takedown of more than 100 websites based on fake court orders, two government officials said.

While online betting is illegal in India, the case has raised concerns that a lack of safeguards in the content takedown system could allow falsified court documents to be used to block legitimate websites.
Modi's office summoned Telecom Secretary Amit Agrawal to appear and explain the lapse, cutting short Agrawal's trip to another state, said the two government officials with knowledge of the matter.

stories.title: ‘Pakistan among most diabetic states’
summary: Professor Dr Javed Akram said on the occasion that around 80 per cent of people in the country were suffering from diabetes, while half of them were unaware that they had developed the disease.

People should remember that diabetes is a silent killer and there is a need to understand the seriousness of the situation and make every possible effort to protect themselves from it." Prof Aftab Mohsin said maintaining a good sleeping routine was extremely important for health.

Managing weight and blood pressure, maintaining a balanced diet and exercising are important for diabetes patients." Prof Khalid Mahmood said there was a need to maintain a balanced diet and reduce the consumption of sugar and salt in daily meals.

stories.title: As smog hangs over Lahore, new pollution squad races to douse stubble fires
summary: Read: Lahore tops global pollution rankings as AQI crosses 500 in several Punjab cities The unit ​is the first of its kind in Pakistan dedicated to fighting pollution, officials say, and it is one of ⁠the most visible steps in a campaign that Punjab officials claim is working.
Farmers caught burning stubble face fines of 15,000 Pakistani rupees ($54) ‌per ⁠acre, said Muhammad Farooq, an assistant director of the Punjab Agriculture Department.
Also read: Punjab blames India's Diwali fireworks for Lahore's toxic air India's foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

stories.title: Pakistan needs 'middle-power alliances' to navigate emerging world order, US-China rivalry
summary: Pakistan would need to forge alliances and partnerships with "like-minded" middle powers to navigate the emerging world order and resist pressure to pick sides in the US-China rivalry.
Read: A world of blocs: where Pakistan stands The professor expounded: “Pakistan needs to form alliances with like-minded countries to be able to withstand pressure from great powers.

The professor added that unlike the Cold War, where countries fell neatly into one camp or another, in the current bipolar dispensation, most countries were “hedging their bets” and were looking for a “better offer” from either the US or China.
